notes.title: Minor Bug Fix – Health Display
notes.notes: Bug Fix – The health numbers on your character sheet were not updating as expected alongside the health boxes when you used medical supplies.  This has been corrected.

notes.title: Blissful Ignorance Bug Fix
notes.notes:
Good morning!  Thanks to a report by a player, some bugs with the game have been corrected.  These are:

*  The achievement 'Why Would You Do This?' was unreachable.  This was caused by the game not running the code for unlocking page-specific achievements if the player died, instead only running the death achievement.

*  Two of the hard unlocks were not pointing to the correct pages in the encyclopedia.  Instead of pointing to the first page of that entry, they loaded the second, and the second page pointed to itself.  This was due to an error in the ordering of the pages in the handler.

Both of these issues have now been taken care of and a new build uploaded.  I cannot thank the player enough and will be emailing them shortly to make sure they know that their contribution and support is of great value to us here at Grindwheel Games.  The same goes for all of our community, as everything from reviews to reports of issues like this help to build the foundations which support the ongoing series.

Have a great weekend!

Tony Wilson - Grindwheel Games

notes.title: In-Game Art Release 6
notes.notes:
Good morning and happy Friday!  The final image for Blissful Ignorance is here.  As with the previous games, this is the 'game over' image you will see when you (inevitably) perish.  It also fits nicely with the theme of books and reading that the other images in the game build.  I hope you enjoy it, and have a great weekend!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35938961/559d106679e5fce30b741da2dded880470fd3863.jpg[/img]

A hunter's story quite often does not have a happy ending. Injury and death are a constant danger in their profession, as are more subtle foes like madness and despair. In many cases the best that they can expect is a temporary reprieve from the gruelling combat and soul-shredding darkness. A morbid sense of humour always helps, of course.

notes.title: In-Game Art Release 5
notes.notes:
Sorry this is a little late today.  Between a Steam issue and a bricked computer we've had to wait until now to bring you today's update.

There is just another 8 days until Halloween and the release of Blissful Ignorance.  With everything set from our end, we invite you to enjoy our latest page art reveal below.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35938961/b23499b499d65ec7ee67dda50afecd2e22511dcb.jpg[/img]

Hunters keep extensive notes on the beasts they have faced in case such beings should reappear in later times. Even mundane outbreaks of ravenous undead are recorded and analysed to give the next generation even a fractional advantage under similar situations. When on the trail of a particularly dangerous foe, any hunter with common sense will consult these extensive, often poorly catalogued archives.

notes.title: In-Game Art Release 4
notes.notes:
Good morning!  I hope you all had a great weekend.  Work has progressed rapidly on the next game in the series, which means that we may be able to see a Halloween launch every year with some luck.  Regardless, Blissful Ignorance is ready to go on all platforms.  Please enjoy today's general page image below!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35938961/acbab518143e84a77cfa4a9306aadcf4efac9e16.jpg[/img]

The UIC is faced with a quandary when it comes to information. Some facts are simply too horrific for the average person to know without sowing panic through the population. But, at the same time, these things cannot be excised and forgotten in case they turn out to be useful. Anyone but a licensed scholar, hunter, or priest that tried to gain access to these dreadful secrets would face the highest of sanctions. But then again, some argue that consulting the works fettered in these dungeons is a dreadful punishment in itself.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35938961/610274d85a13136f1138c6e7f624a3a83e04c7f4.jpg[/img]

Gazing Upon the Abyss is a collection of short poems that caused some controversy when it was released. Many of the contributors had spent time 'recovering' in Bedlam houses, or were otherwise known to be of a morbid disposition. A keen-eyed hunter who purchased the book noticed certain references to forbidden knowledge in one poem, and the writer was subsequently discovered to be a worshipper of the Bleak Gods. As can be seen here, the owner of this copy has rightly locked it in a cabinet to prevent unwary readers being exposed to the contents.

The Illustrated Anatomy series covers the most commonly found creatures, natural and unnatural, that can be found in the world.  This volume, dealing with Harpies and other avian menaces, was recalled and censored when it was discovered that the author had inserted a chapter claiming that pureblood humans and Harpies are related through a common ancestor.  Interestingly, this copy contains this section without alteration.

Tales of the Hungry Desert was initially sold as a true account of the fall of the Ochre Kingdoms upon release. However, glaring inaccuracies in everything from religious practices to place names caused outrage in the Calif-In-Exile's court. To avoid a diplomatic incident the author was questioned, and admitted that the work was actually a satire of UIC politics. After paying a significant fine and printing an apology, all copies of the book that could be found were amended to note that they were works of fiction. This rare copy does not contain the retraction.
